title: Graded liveness checks and backoff windows for SLO-aware load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are seeing autoscaler thrash and cross-region failover churn when transient backend degradation triggers binary liveness probes. This causes capacity oscillation that violates tail latency SLOs for customers in affected regions and can cascade into global capacity pressure.

Context: Current readiness/liveness is a hard pass/fail per-instance probe evaluated every 5s with a 3-failure kill. In multi-zone clusters this produces correlated instance removals during brief packet loss spikes or GC pauses. Autoscaler reacts to the sudden drop in healthy endpoints, scales up, then scales down when probes recover, creating spikes in cold-start latency and increased token cost.

Goal: Replace the binary probe model with a graded liveness check plus backoff windows and short-term autoscaler derating so that transient degradations do not trigger large scale changes. The fix must be safe for multi-region failover and compatible with existing circuit breaker policies and rollout controls.
proposal_summary: Introduce a multi-stage probe outcome (OK, Degraded, Unhealthy) based on latency and error-rate buckets. Maintain a short soft-fail window where instances marked Degraded are kept but subjected to traffic steering and reduced load via client-side load-shedding signals. Only transition to Unhealthy for sustained failures across a configurable sampling window. Tie the autoscaler to a health-quorum metric (percentage of OK nodes) with a derating factor to prevent immediate aggressive scale-ups when quorum briefly drops. Integrate with circuit breaker to trigger regional routing changes when majority Unhealthy counts persist.
acceptance_criteria: New probe returns one of OK/Degraded/Unhealthy and is available behind feature flag
Autoscaler respects health-quorum and applies configurable derating before scaling decisions
No regression in stable cluster CPU and memory usage after rollout (<=5% change in baseline over 24h)
Observed reduction in autoscaler-induced instance churn during simulated transient network blips (>=50% decrease)
End-to-end test coverage for probe state transitions and interaction with circuit breaker and routing policies
Runbook updated with new recovery steps and troubleshooting queries
implementation_plan: WIP: Instrument graded probe library (eng/runtime/probes). Initial API: probe.check() -> {status: 'OK'|'DEGRADED'|'UNHEALTHY', reason: string, metric_tags: []}
Add client-side routing hook: when status==DEGRADED, lower routing weight and enable token-level shed signals
Autoscaler: add health-quorum input (rolling % of OK nodes) and derating multiplier in scale-up policy
Circuit breaker: extend to listen for region-level Unhealthy ratio and initiate failover flows after sustained threshold
Feature-flag rollout: phasing per-region, start staging -> canary (10%) -> region-wide with 24h observation windows
Docs: console runbook, observability dashboard tiles, and API changelog
metrics_and_alerting: Degraded ratio: track % of instances in DEGRADED state, alert if >10% sustained for 5m
Autoscaler scale events per minute: reduce target change frequency by >=50% during chaos tests
Tail P95/P99 latency per-region: must not degrade by >10% after rollout
Cold-starts per 10k requests: monitor for increases and alert at >2x baseline
rollout_plan: Stage: Implement library behind ff/runtime/graded-probes in staging cluster (2026-03-05 to 2026-03-09)
Canary: Enable in us-west-2 with 10% of traffic for 48h, run chaos test (packet loss and gc pauses) and validate metrics (2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13)
Region expansion: Enable in additional regions sequentially (EU/US-EAST/APAC) with 24h holds between regions
Full rollout gated by: no increase in customer-impacting latencies, autoscaler churn reduction verified, runbook & monitoring green
Rollback: revert feature flag, disable health-quorum influence on autoscaler, and restore binary probe behavior
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed for probe API. Prototype shows stable classification for 95% of transient GC events in local sim. - Aisha

2026-03-04: Design review with SRE and runtime teams. Decision: initial Degraded threshold = latency >150ms OR error-rate >1% for 30s sampling window. Action: add configurable sampling windows per deployment. - Marco
2026-03-06: Implemented probe library and unit tests. Pushed feature branch runtime/graded-probes. Basic integration tests passing in containerized environment. - Marco

2026-03-08: Autoscaler team implemented health-quorum input and added derating multiplier (0.5 by default) for first scale-up decision. Need e2e test to ensure no starvation when many pods are legitimately unhealthy. - Priya (autoscaler)

2026-03-11: Canary started in us-west-2 with 10% traffic. Early telemetry: degraded-ratio peaked at 7% during a small network flake and recovered without triggering scale-up. Tail latency unchanged. Continuing observation for 48h. - Marco
2026-03-10: Added runbook draft and troubleshooting queries (Kusto/PromQL) for probe states and quorum evaluation. - Aisha
notes:
Trade-offs: Graded probes add complexity to probe logic and increase surface area for misconfiguration. We prefer conservative defaults and feature flags to limit blast radius. Autoscaler derating reduces sensitivity, which could delay necessary scale-up under true demand spikes; mitigate by bounding derating duration and combining with request-rate signals.

Open questions: exact sampling window for global clusters vs small clusters, how to surface Degraded nodes in Console (UI tile vs logs), and whether to allow per-customer override for private deployments.
qa_checks: Unit tests for probe state machine (100% branch coverage)
Integration test: simulated packet loss 2s bursts, verify no autoscaler scale-up (10 runs)
Load test: 1h at 2x normal traffic with canary behavior enabled, monitor cold-starts and p99
